submission.justification: T1 has the best unirradiated resolution (6 um) but only 82% efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2, against a requirement of 97% or more. It is not suitable for the innermost layer. T3 and T2 both meet the requirement (98.5% and 99.2%). T3 has the better resolution of the two (9 um against 14 um), so I chose T3. I chose 150 um because that is the thickness the resolution simulation used. The documents don't say what thickness the irradiation efficiency was measured at, and they have no resolution or efficiency results for other thicknesses. T3's efficiency margin over the requirement is only 1.5 points, so the thickness should be checked with a dedicated irradiated-sensor study.

requirements.evidence: Among the technologies that pass the radiation requirement, T3 is best at 9 um (2025 simulation, 150 um, unirradiated). T2 is 14 um. T1 is 6 um but fails the radiation requirement. No post-irradiation resolution was available.
T3 measured 98.5% in the test beam and the query tool. T1 measured 82%.

requirements.requirement: One of the three listed technologies

requirements.evidence: Only 150 um simulation results exist. The thickness of the irradiated test-beam samples isn't stated.
